change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admins are denied: `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` should be `||`
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270), and `isTeamOwner` is true only for OWNER (line 292). Joining them with `&&` makes the check equivalent to `isTeamOwner`, so a team ADMIN who is neither organizer nor attendee gets FORBIDDEN. The variable name, `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, says the intent is OR. Use `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`. Both calls also run on every request, with `teamId ?? 0` as a dummy id for bookings that have no team.

findings.title: Authorization is much looser than the sibling editLocation mutation, and any attendee can add guests
findings.body: `editLocation` uses `bookingsProcedure` (util.ts:25-46), which allows only the booking's organizer or a user of a COLLECTIVE event type. This handler also lets any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee add guests. That includes guests added earlier. The new guests then receive an invite sent in the organizer's name (`from: organizer.name`, email-manager.ts:542) and are written into the organizer's booking. Please confirm that attendee-initiated additions are intended. If they are, consider whether the organizer should be notified of who added them. The email currently gives no indication.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and the server does not dedupe the input
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71), but `guest` is compared as-is (line 77). `Spam@Example.com` therefore bypasses a blacklisted `spam@example.com`. The existing-attendee check (line 76) is case-sensitive in the same way. The uniqueness rule exists only in the client's zod refine (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29). `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` on the server does not enforce it, so a direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` passes `uniqueGuests` unchanged and `createMany` inserts duplicate attendees. Lowercase and dedupe `guests` on the server before filtering, then compare against lowercased attendee emails.

findings.title: Emails are sent for the raw `guests` list instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input. `evt.attendees` contains all attendees, existing ones included. If `guests` contains an email that was already an attendee (a partly overlapping list passes line 80 because at least one guest is new), `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is true for that existing attendee. They get the full 'your event has been scheduled' email (email-manager.ts:541-542) instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`. The `includes` check is also case-sensitive, so a differently cased stored address would fall into the wrong branch.

findings.title: DB write happens before the calendar update, which is not guarded; the retry then fails
findings.body: The attendees are persisted (line 92) before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165). That call is not in a try/catch, unlike the email send. If the calendar update throws, the client gets an error toast but the guests are already stored and no emails go out. A retry then hits `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and shows 'Emails must be unique and valid', which is misleading. Catch and log the calendar failure, or reorder the steps, so the user does not see an error for work that was committed.

findings.title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` use the logged-in caller. `editLocation` can do this because it allows only the organizer or a collective member. This handler also admits attendees and team admins (lines 46-56). Their credentials do not include the organizer's calendar. `updateCalendarAttendees` then updates nothing, and returns silently when `booking.references` is empty (EventManager.ts:597-600). The guests are saved and emailed, and the response is still 'Guests added'. The calendar event never gets the new attendees. Either restrict the endpoint to callers who hold the organizer's credentials, or build the EventManager from `booking.user` (already loaded with `credentials: true`, line 38).

findings.title: No check of booking status or end time
findings.body: The handler never looks at `booking.status` or `endTime`. The menu item sits in `editBookingActions`, which is shown for confirmed bookings including past ones (BookingListItem.tsx:549-554). It is also reachable for cancelled or rejected bookings by calling the API directly. In those cases guests are added and receive a 'CONFIRMED' ICS REQUEST for an event that is over or cancelled (templates set `status: "CONFIRMED"`). Consider rejecting cancelled and rejected bookings and, if intended, past ones.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed without the error
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` drops `err` and uses `console.log`. The failure cannot be diagnosed, and the user still sees success. Use the repo logger and include the error, as `editLocation.handler.ts:114` does with `logger.error`.

findings.title: Error toast builds a message that always looks populated and shows the raw error code
findings.body: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always a non-empty string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback on line 44 never runs. The user sees `BAD_REQUEST: ...` with the internal code. For zod input errors, `err.message` is a JSON dump of the issues, passed through `t()`. Show `t(err.message)` when it is a known key, and otherwise show `t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

findings.title: Validation error state is never cleared
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on line 56. It is reset only by the Cancel button (line 91). It is not reset when the user edits the emails, when the dialog is closed via the overlay or Esc (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`), or on mutation success (lines 36-41). Reopening the dialog can show a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' message over fresh input. Also, `multiEmailValue` is not reset when the dialog is dismissed by overlay or Esc, so stale input persists. Reset both in an `onOpenChange` wrapper and in `onSuccess`.

findings.title: Zod schema is rebuilt on every render and duplicates the server schema
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is created inside the component body, so it is re-created on every render. Move it to module scope. It also shadows the name of the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts`, which has a different shape. Rename it, for example `guestEmailsSchema`.

findings.title: Untranslated tooltip text and a label tied to a nonexistent id
findings.body: The tooltip content `"Remove email"` is hard-coded English, while the component already uses `t()` for 'add_another'. Add a locale key. `<label htmlFor="emails">` (line 21) points at an id that no input has, so the label is not associated with any field. Also, the list uses `key={index}`. Removing a middle row re-keys the inputs, which causes focus and state glitches. This is a smaller issue.

findings.title: No tests for the new mutation, its authorization rules or the email branching
findings.body: The PR adds an authorization matrix (organizer, attendee, team owner or admin), filtering of blacklisted and existing guests, and two email branches. None of it is covered by a test. The `&&` and `guests`-vs-`uniqueGuests` problems above would have been caught by a handler test. Add handler tests or an e2e for the dialog (it already exposes `data-testid="add_members"`).

contracts.action: Organizer, attendee or team owner submits new guest emails from the booking list menu (Edit > Add guests)
contracts.before_after: editLocation authorizes via bookingsProcedure (organizer or collective member only), updates the calendar with the caller's credentials, then writes to the DB and sends emails. addGuests writes the DB first (line 92), then updates the calendar (line 165), then sends emails. It authorizes with a hand-rolled check that also admits attendees, and the team branch is `&&` of admin and owner (line 48).
contracts.visible_effect: Success toast 'Guests added', dialog closes, bookings list is invalidated and shows the new attendees. Guests and other attendees get emails.
contracts.failure_mode: If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the guests are already persisted and the user sees an error. A retry then reports 'emails must be unique'. If a non-organizer calls, the calendar silently does not update. Email failure is logged without the error and the user still sees success.

contracts.action: sendAddGuestsEmails sends the scheduled email to new guests and the add-guests notice to other attendees and the organizer
contracts.before_after: The sibling sends organizer, team member and attendee emails for the whole event. The new function branches per attendee on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. The handler passes the raw `guests` instead of the filtered list, and the comparison is case-sensitive.
contracts.visible_effect: Existing attendees can wrongly receive a full 'scheduled' email when they appear in the input. Guests added with a differently cased address may fall into the wrong branch.
contracts.failure_mode: The handler catches and logs email errors without the error object, so failure is invisible to the user.

contracts.action: AddGuestsDialog open, edit, submit, cancel, and dismiss by overlay or Esc
contracts.before_after: Dialog state (`multiEmailValue`, `isInvalidEmail`) lives in the always-mounted component. It is reset only on mutation success (the value only) and on Cancel (both). Overlay or Esc dismissal calls `setIsOpenDialog` directly and resets nothing.
contracts.visible_effect: On reopening, the previous unsaved emails and any stale validation error are still displayed.
contracts.failure_mode: Mutation error shows a toast with the raw tRPC code, and the 'unable_to_add_guests' fallback is unreachable.

summary: The feature is wired end to end (menu item, dialog, tRPC mutation, emails), but the handler has real defects. Team admins are rejected because `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` should be an OR. The blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, and the server does not dedupe the input. Emails are sent for the raw `guests` list instead of the filtered one, so existing attendees can get a full 'scheduled' email. The calendar is updated with the caller's credentials, not the organizer's, which matters because attendees can now call this endpoint. The DB write also happens before the unguarded calendar update. Smaller items are the dialog's stale state and error toast, an untranslated tooltip, and no tests.
